The same voice names the daughter-of-Zion formula at web:Lam.1.6 inside “All majesty has departed from the daughter of Zion.” web:Lam.1.6 (this verse also carries a ketiv/qere note per the inventory, not engaged by the present reading; the formula itself recurs seven further times book-wide, sweep: 8 verses book-wide), and keeps the same distance through the roads, gates and priests of web:Lam.1.4. The report closes on “She has no comforter.” web:Lam.1.9 immediately followed by the first-person plea “See, Yahweh, my affliction; for the enemy has magnified himself.” web:Lam.1.9, a brief intrusion of Zion's own voice inside an otherwise third-person span (a per-bytes deviation from a plain city_lament reading, disclosed rather than smoothed over). The same verse completes the contiguous refrain אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier; roughly "she is without a comforter"; sweep of the two-word refrain: 3 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), and refrains close units under the owner-ruled seam law: the boundary sits here rather than folding this verse forward with the interjection that follows it.
